headline: Computational models predict cell fate and state from single-cell and atlas data
label: Predictive Models Of Cell Fate
summary: Single-cell atlases now support generative and information-theoretic models that forecast cell fate, from mouse embryos to tumours and organoid surrogates.
synthesis: The common thread is predictive modeling of cell state and fate built on large single-cell and atlas resources. Navigo applies generative flow matching with RNA kinetics modeling to learn developmental vector fields from a 12.4M-cell mouse embryo scRNA-seq atlas. FateLimit takes an information-theoretic view, quantifying when single-cell omics data make future fate predictable and introducing a fate half-life. V3Cell instead builds in silico 3D organoid surrogates from bright-field microscopy to predict developmental fate and perturbation responses. Reference-building work supplies the substrate: a 94-cell-type healthy pancreas framework from 815,126 transcriptomes across 109 donors, and a replicability assessment of mouse brain cell clusters across two atlases exceeding 4M cells. What is new is explicit quantification of predictability limits and the extension of fate modeling to imaging-derived surrogates.
